page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-224 is a general-purpose virtual machine designed for high-density, compute-heavy, and distributed enterprise workloads. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it is powered by AMD EPYC 7B13 processors, providing 112 dedicated physical cores and 224 virtual CPUs via simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation is balanced at 896 GB of system RAM, maintaining the standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 4 GB per virtual core. Cache structure features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. Hardware acceleration extensions include AVX, AES, VAES, SHA-NI, and BMI2, though AVX-512 instructions are unsupported on this architecture.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional multi-threaded capabilities, placing the instance in the top 10% for both stress-ng multi-core throughput and PassMark CPU metrics, including encryption and extended instruction tests. Cached small-block memory bandwidth exceeds 12.5 TB/sec, complementing strong large-block uncached read and write speeds. In-memory data structures perform effectively, evidenced by Redis SET operations reaching top-tier throughput. Single-core execution across Geekbench and stress-ng falls within average to strong brackets, while software compilation and image processing demonstrate strong throughput.

The server does not include bundled local storage or dedicated hardware accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage and standard network interfaces without complimentary public IPv4 addresses. While raw CPU inference can handle smaller parameter models, larger generative AI tasks show steep throughput degradation due to the lack of dedicated GPU resources.

The n2d-standard-224 provides an efficient resource profile for organizations requiring high core density without the pricing premium associated with extreme memory-optimized or GPU instances. Its balanced resource footprint is suited for distributed enterprise databases, large-scale Clang compilation jobs, in-memory caching tiers, static web fleets, and parallel scientific computing pipelines.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-224 is a high-density general-purpose virtual machine equipped with 224 vCPUs and 896 GB of system memory, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Built on AMD EPYC 7B13 x86_64 processors across 112 dedicated physical cores, it supports hardware cryptography, AVX, and BMI2 instructions. Benchmarks place this instance in the top 10% for multi-core compute and PassMark CPU evaluations, alongside top-tier memory caching throughput and high Redis operation rates. The configuration includes no integrated local storage or GPUs, relying on attached storage solutions. Given its significant thread density and multi-core scaling, the n2d-standard-224 delivers qualitative cost efficiency for highly parallelized workloads, making it well suited for large compilation pipelines, enterprise in-memory caches, distributed databases, and high-throughput web serving infrastructure.
